timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: How do big services stay up under a million users?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Load balancing, failover, and autoscaling. The holy trinity of availability.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Spreads traffic across healthy instances and routes around failures.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Redundancy. When a node, zone, or region fails, traffic shifts to a standby.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Add or remove capacity with demand. Reactive or predictive. Match load exactly.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Failure isolation. One zone dying shouldn't kill the app. Regions give disaster recovery.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Accept partial failures. Minimize service loss. Degrade gracefully.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Service-level objectives. Availability is only real if you measure it.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So one instance is never the answer?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: One instance is a single point of failure. Availability is a design, not a setting.
